Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The umpires and the players are set on the field to start the run chase. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma are the opening batters for India Women. Ayabonga Khaka to start the new ball attack for South Africa Women. Let's Play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

With a modest target of 85 runs to win, India Women are in a strong position to level the series. Their bowlers have laid the foundation with a superb performance, and now it’s up to the batters to chase down the total and avoid a series loss. Stay tuned as we bring you the second innings.

Arundhati Reddy is in for a chat. She says that this was a complete performance and it is a great sign going ahead. Adds that they were not up to the mark where they wanted to be in the last couple of games. Shares that she focused on her strengths and kept it stump-to-stump. Tells that the wicket was on the slower side and she had to adjust accordingly. Feels that the turn and bounce on offer helped the bowlers.

South Africa Women, after being put in to bat, struggled from the outset. Their innings began on a shaky note when skipper Laura Wolvaardt was dismissed for nine in the fourth over. Marizanne Kapp then joined Tazmin Brits, who looked promising at the crease. However, Kapp couldn't make an impact and was sent back to the pavilion for 10. The Proteas Women ended the powerplay at 39/2, with Anneke Bosch coming in at number four. Deepti Sharma made an immediate impact by dismissing the in-form Tazmin Brits for 20 in her very first over. The Indian bowlers swiftly wrapped up the tail, bowling out South Africa Women for a mere 84 runs. Pooja Vastrakar was the standout performer for India, claiming her career-best T20I figures of 4/13. Radha Yadav was equally impressive, picking up three wickets for just six runs in her three overs. Arundhati Reddy, Shreyanka Patil, and Deepti Sharma contributed with a wicket each, completing a dominant bowling display.

It's all over and India Women have bowled out South Africa Women for just 84 runs. Superb commitment by India Women from the word GO! They have been electric in the field and have grabbed every opportunity that came their way. A series finale and the right time for Pooja Vastrakar and Radha Yadav to shine bright with 4 and 3 wickets respectively along with Arundhati Reddy getting a couple. An innings belonging only to India Women as they swept the South Africa Women batters away for just 84 runs.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! All over for South Africa Women! A job well done by India Women. Opens the bat face to steer it down to deep third but ends up getting a feather on it and the keeper, Uma Chetry does the rest. Pooja Vastrakar ends with career-best T20I figures of 3.1-0-13-4. South Africa Women bowled out for 84.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness to get the series finale underway. A decent crowd is already in and more should trickle in as the night progresses. Harmanpreet Kaur leads her troops out to the centre, followed by the two openers of South Africa Women. It will be Laura Wolvaardt and Tazmin Brits to open the innings for the visitors. Pooja Vastrakar has the new ball in hand and she is raring to go. Off we go...

PITCH REPORT - Shebani Bhaskar is near the deck. She starts by saying that this is the same surface that was used in the last game. Tells that the Indian spinners pulled their lengths back towards the end, which allowed them to limit South Africa, and bowling similar lengths would be key in this game. Opines that this is a brilliant track to bat and does not have too many cracks. Informs that there is a forecast for rain later in the night, and that would have influenced the decision at the toss. States that there was extra bounce in the last clash, and the ground staff reckons that there will be more of the same. Ends by saying that 180-190 might be a good score on this wicket.

The skipper of South Africa Women, Laura Wolvaardt says that they were looking to bat first. Adds that this is the third game on the same wicket and have done well in the last couple of games while batting first, which is why they wanted to bat first. States that she was pleased with the effort of the batters in the second game because the wicket was on the slower side. Further says that a series win would be the cherry on top before the World Cup. Shares that this is the last game for them to try a couple of things. Informs that they are going with the same team as the last game.

The captain of India Women, Harmanpreet Kaur says that looking at the conditions of the ground and the wicket, with the dew coming down in the second innings, they would want to bowl. She adds that they were in the game till the 18th over in the previous game and things changed from there. She further says that they have no changes in the playing XI.

South Africa Women (Unchanged Playing XI) - Laura Wolvaardt (C), Tazmin Brits, Marizanne Kapp, Anneke Bosch, Chloe Tryon, Nadine de Klerk, Annerie Dercksen, Eliz-Mari Marx, Sinalo Jafta (WK), Ayabonga Khaka, Nonkululeko Mlaba.

India Women (Unchanged Playing XI) - Shafali Verma, Smriti Mandhana, Sajeevan Sajana, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Jemimah Rodrigues, Uma Chetry (WK), Deepti Sharma, Pooja Vastrakar, Radha Yadav, Shreyanka Patil, Arundhati Reddy.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in the favour of Harmanpreet Kaur. India Women have opted to BOWL first.

This match is a do-or-die situation for India, and they will be banking on their experienced players to rise to the occasion. Harmanpreet Kaur's leadership will be crucial, and she will need to inspire her team to deliver a cohesive performance. The Indian batters will also need to bring their A-game, ensuring they set or chase a competitive total against a formidable South African side. As the teams take the field, the stage is set for a gripping finale. Will South Africa seal the series, or will India bounce back to level it? Stay tuned as we bring you all the excitement along with the toss and team news.

South Africa comes into this match with their confidence bolstered by their victory in the first T20I, where they posted a commanding score of 177 runs. Opener Tazmin Brits has been in scintillating form, scoring 81 and 52 in the two matches so far. Her aggressive batting at the top of the order has been instrumental in setting up strong starts for her team. The Proteas will be looking to her once again to provide a solid foundation and hope for a similar performance from their batters in this clash. On the other hand, the Indian team, led by Harmanpreet Kaur, has had a challenging series with their bowlers struggling to find their rhythm. Despite this, the Indian team is determined to put up a strong fight and level the series. The Indian bowlers will need to step up and deliver incisive spells to contain the South African batters, who have been in impressive form. Adding to India’s challenges are the fitness concerns with key players. Richa Ghosh, who was hit on the head in the first T20I, is still recovering, while Dayalan Hemalatha missed the second match due to an ankle injury. Their availability remains uncertain, and the Indian team management might have to stick with the same XI unless one or both of them are declared fit to play.

A warm welcome to all our viewers as we bring you the thrilling finale of the T20 series between the Indian Women and the South Africa Women at the iconic M.A. Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai. The series has been a roller-coaster ride with South Africa currently leading 1-0, and India fighting to level the series in this decisive third T20I. The second T20I was washed out due to rain, leaving India with only one opportunity to square the series. Fingers crossed for better weather for this game as fans eagerly anticipate an exciting contest.
... MATCH DAY ...

The final game of South Africa Women's long and engrossing tour of India is here. In the 3rd and final T20I, India Women go up against South Africa Women at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai. The Proteas Women currently lead the three-match series 1-0 after notching up a stellar win in the first game and then we only saw one team bat in the second game as persistent rain blew away any chances of there being a series decider in the final game. South Africa Women haven't had their best time in India on this tour so far given they lost the ODI series 3-0 and then the solo Test match as well but their performances haven't been bad by any means. They have simply been outplayed on the big occasions for most of the series and in the one and a half T20I games we've seen, their luck has started to get a bit better as well. Tazmin Brits has really been the star with the bat for them in both matches thus far and her hitting prowess makes such a huge difference especially up top as it allows Laura Wolvaardt to play her classy strokes and not worry too much about the scoring rate. There is some depth in the batting and won't be expected to make more than a change or so if they decide to bring Sune Luus. Marizanne Kapp is the impactful all-rounder in the side and the likes of Ayabonga Khaka and Masabata Klaas provide good depth to the bowling attack. India on the other hand made four changes to the Playing XI after losing the first game and only one of them was forced as Uma Chetry came in for Richa Ghosh who had some issues with a concussion in the first game. Frontline pacer Renuka Singh was dropped and so were a couple of others and the fact that they didn't get a chance to bat in the previous game, we might see a similarly constituted team. For the first time on this tour, Harmanpreet Kaur and her warriors are staring in the face of a series defeat and they can only at best get back on level terms which makes this match an even more exciting watch. Who are you backing for the win?
